title: Guests said the hotel water tasted strange...
note: The Cecil Hotel, told respectfully: no gore, no ghost hype, the coroner's ruling stated plainly, the internet-sleuth harm as the cautionary turn, and the 2021 affordable-housing reopening as the ending. Facts and sources: shorts/edits_movie/cecil_hotel.script.md. Run from the work folder holding src/ and tx/.

beats.say: In February 2013, guests at a Los Angeles hotel complained the water tasted strange. And the water pressure was terrible.
beats.speak: In February twenty thirteen, guests at a Los Angeles hotel complained the water tasted strange. And the water pressure was terrible.

beats.say: So a maintenance worker went up to the roof, and checked the four water tanks.
Inside one of them, he found a missing guest. Elisa Lam, a twenty-one-year-old student from Vancouver.
beats.speak: Inside one of them, he found a missing guest. Eleesa Lam, a twenty-one-year-old student from Vancouver.

beats.say: She had vanished almost three weeks earlier. And hundreds of people had been using that water.
To find her, police had released her last video, from the hotel's elevator. It spread around the world.
But the bookstore manager who met her on her last day remembers her very differently.
And people noticed where she had stayed. The Cecil Hotel. It opened in 1924, and became one of the most notorious buildings in Los Angeles.
beats.speak: And people noticed where she had stayed. The Cecil Hotel. It opened in nineteen twenty-four, and became one of the most notorious buildings in Los Angeles.

beats.say: The serial killer known as the Night Stalker is said to have lived there in 1985. And in 1991, an Austrian serial killer, working as a journalist, checked in too.
beats.speak: The serial killer known as the Night Stalker is said to have lived there in nineteen eighty-five. And in nineteen ninety-one, an Austrian serial killer, working as a journalist, checked in too.

beats.say: So the internet decided it had to be something dark. Ghosts. Cover-ups. Murder. Online sleuths even named a suspect: a heavy-metal musician who had stayed there a year earlier.
He was in Mexico, recording an album, and he could prove it. Years later, he still gets hate messages.
The real answer was much sadder. Elisa had bipolar disorder, and the coroner ruled her death an accidental drowning.
beats.speak: The real answer was much sadder. Eleesa had bipolar disorder, and the coroner ruled her death an accidental drowning.

beats.say: In 2021, the Cecil reopened. Not as a hotel, but as six hundred homes for people with nowhere else to go.
beats.speak: In twenty twenty-one, the Cecil reopened. Not as a hotel, but as six hundred homes for people with nowhere else to go.

beats.say: So the hotel the internet called haunted, now gives people a home. Remember Elisa kindly.
beats.speak: So the hotel the internet called haunted, now gives people a home. Remember Eleesa kindly.
